questions.answer: Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$: $2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x}{y}$.

questions.q: Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ given $x^3+y^3=6xy$, and evaluate it at the point $(3,3)$.
Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ given $y^2-xy+x^2=7$, and evaluate it at the point $(1,3)$.
A curve is defined parametrically by $x=t^2$, $y=2t^3$. Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$.
A curve is defined by $x=3\cos t$, $y=3\sin t$. Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$, and find the gradient at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-3\sin t$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3\cos t$. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3\cos t}{-3\sin t}=-\cot t$. At $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $-\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=-1$, since $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

questions.q: A spherical balloon is inflated so its volume increases at a constant rate of $100$ cm$^3$/s. Find the rate of increase of the radius when $r=5$ cm, using $V=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, to three decimal places.
The area of a circular ripple increases at $8\pi$ cm$^2$/s. Find the rate of change of the radius when $r=4$ cm, using $A=\pi r^2$.

A cone-shaped tank (vertex down) has height $10$ cm and top radius $4$ cm, so at water depth $h$ the radius is $r=\dfrac{2h}{5}$. Water is poured in at $12$ cm$^3$/s. Find the rate of rise of the water level when $h=5$ cm, using $V=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h$.
The radius of a circular oil slick increases at a constant rate of $0.5$ m/min. Find the rate of increase of its area when $r=20$ m.

Applying the rules: tangents and second derivatives

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent to $y=xe^{-x}$ at $x=1$.
questions.answer: By the product rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{-x}+x(-e^{-x})=e^{-x}(1-x)$. At $x=1$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{-1}(0)=0$. Since $y(1)=e^{-1}$, the tangent is horizontal: $y=\dfrac{1}{e}$.

questions.q: Find $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ for $y=\ln(x^2+1)$, and evaluate it at $x=1$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a ladder sliding down a wall

questions.q: This question has three parts. A ladder $5$ m long leans against a vertical wall, its base on horizontal ground. The base slides away from the wall at a constant rate of $0.4$ m/s. (a) Let $x$ be the distance of the base from the wall and $y$ the height of the top of the ladder. Write the relationship between $x$ and $y$, and differentiate implicitly with respect to time $t$ to relate $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$. (b) Find the rate at which the top of the ladder is sliding down the wall when the base is $3$ m from the wall. (c) Using $x=5\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the ladder and the ground, find the rate at which $\theta$ is changing at that instant.
questions.answer: (a) $x^2+y^2=25$. Differentiating with respect to $t$: $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt}+2y\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-\dfrac{x}{y}\dfrac{dx}{dt}$. (b) When $x=3$, $y=\sqrt{25-9}=4$. $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-\dfrac{3}{4}(0.4)=-0.3$ m/s, so the top slides down at $0.3$ m/s. (c) Differentiating $x=5\cos\theta$: $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-5\sin\theta\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$. At this instant $\sin\theta=\dfrac{y}{5}=\dfrac{4}{5}=0.8$, so $0.4=-5(0.8)\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=-4\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$, giving $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=-0.1$ rad/s (the angle is decreasing).
